messages:
chris: Quick sync — we have 3 customer-driven asks that want expedited onboarding paths into the model catalog this sprint. can we triage and pick what actually fits the Q2 roadmap?
maya: list them pls
chris: 1) Enterprise A: needs a pinned model variant with guaranteed latency SLA + audit logs; 2) StartUp B: wants faster onramp with lightweight benchmark pass (no long evals); 3) Platform partner C: requests automated compatibility shim for a custom tokenization edge-case
oliver: rough impact estimates?
chris: Enterprise A = high scope (dedicated infra + SLA), StartUp B = low scope but high velocity, Partner C = medium scope (engineering adapter + validation).
tasha: can we reuse the lightweight benchmark harness from last quarter for StartUp B? that'd save ~2 weeks.
maya: yes, we have a trimmed harness that checks latency/ppl/zero-shot sanity only — no full evals. good candidate.
oliver: risk matrix idea: severity vs effort. My vote: fast follow StartUp B to show quick wins, parallelize discovery for Partner C, gate Enterprise A behind contract + infra budget.
chris: agreed but Enterprise A is a big logo, sales pushing. what are minimum launch acceptance criteria we can present to them without promising infra changes?
tasha: propose this MEA (Minimum External Acceptance):
- model pinned to catalog with version label
- basic perf bench: 95th latency under X ms for 512 tokens on standard instance
- audit logs exported to S3 with 30d retention
- documented fallback variant (lower-cost) if SLA breached
chris: that seems doable. but pinned + SLA implies Dedicated capacity or reserved routing — we should be explicit about the contract ask.
maya: flag to sales_bot: request contract language: "reserved throughput or defined latency SLO; credits/penalty clause; onboarding window". sales_bot: noted, will loop in AE Taylor.
oliver: for Partner C compatibility shim — can we scope it as an adapter layer that rewrites tokenization at request time and runs a short conv-check harness? estimate 1.5 sprint dev + 1 sprint QA.
tasha: plus we need a canary rollout plan: start with internal-only, then 5% partner traffic, monitor hallucination/regression metrics for 48h, then 20%.
chris: add fallback routing: if regression > threshold, auto-failover to baseline model and alert on-call.
maya: backlog items (short names):
- B-onramp-trim-harness
- C-token-adapter-poc
- A-contract-edge-sla
- canary-runbook-and-alerting
oliver: prioritize order: B-onramp-trim-harness (P0), A-contract-edge-sla (P1 sales-blocker), canary-runbook (P1), C-token-adapter (P2 exploratory)
tasha: dependencies: eng-infra to confirm reserved routing feasibility (esp for A). Should we request a gating readout from infra by EOD Thursday?
chris: yes — @oliver can you ping eng-infra and ask for confirmation and a short note on estimated ops cost for reserved routing?
oliver: on it. pinged eng-infra channel with summary.
maya: timeline proposal for sprint scope (2-week sprint):
- Week1: B harness + start A contract negotiations + infra feasibility check
- Week2: canary runbook + begin C adapter spike (if infra clear)
chris: comms: tell sales to set customer expectations: demo pinned catalog entry without committed SLA until infra confirmation. that buys us time.
tasha: UX note: catalog UI needs a "customer-pinned" badge and a simple SLA summary view. small UI change — 3-4 pts.
chris: ok add ui-pinned-badge to backlog (P1 for Enterprise A).
maya: acceptance criteria checklist for StartUp B quick onramp:
- trimmed harness passed
- example client integration doc
- 1 internal canary OK for 24h
- no blocker bugs
chris: final: action items assigned — B harness -> maya; A contract -> chris+sales; infra ask -> oliver; canary runbook -> tasha; C adapter spike -> oliver (if infra green). I'll post an update to the roadmap doc after infra reply.
maya: cool. +1
oliver: noted. will update eng-infra thread with cost numbers and ETA.
tasha: i'll sketch canary playbook and minimal UI mock for the pinned badge by Thurs.
sales_bot: AE Taylor assigned, will reach out to Enterprise A with proposed MEA language and timeline.
chris: thanks everyone. landing note: if infra says reserved routing is >2 sprints, we pivot and offer a soft SLA (SLA-lite) with customer-facing expectations and prioritized migration path. fine?
maya: fine. let's reconvene Thu 3pm if we have infra readout.
chris: meeting scheduled. thanks.
